texts.facts: This petition is filed under Section 438 Cr.P.C. seeking anticipatory bail for release of the petitioner in the event of his arrest registered in Crime No.70/2020 of Athani Police Station for the offences punishable under Section 272, 273, 328 of I.P.C. and under Sections 54, 57, 59 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Food Safety and Standards Rules-2011. 2. The facts briefly stated in the petition are that, on the complaint filed by A.S.I., Athani Police Station, criminal case is registered, wherein the petitioner is arrayed as accused No.2. The allegations are that on the directions of C.P.I., Athani Circle, the complainant-ASI and other police officials conducted raid in the farmhouse in R.S.No.107/1+2/1(b) at Aralihatti village, where accused No.1 was involved in making adulteration in order to increase the quantity of milk by making use of hazardous materials. On enquiry, it was learnt that accused No.2 was supplying the said hazardous materials for adulteration. On registering the complaint, the police officials are making attempts to arrest the petitioner. 3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner-accused No.2 and the learned HCGP for the respondents-State. No cogent material has been seized at the time of raid to show that accused No.2-petitioner has supplied the hazardous materials. Accused No.1 has been granted regular bail.
texts.arguments: 4. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that when the police have conducted raid, the petitioner was not found at the spot, it is only on the information said to have been disclosed by accused No.1, the petitioner is falsely implicated as accused No.2. In the event of arrest and detention, the petitioner will be put to great hardship. 5. Per contra, the learned HCGP submitted that at the time of raid, the hazardous materials which are used for adulteration have been seized, accused Nos.1 and 2 are involved in the illegal activities, which affects the health of people consuming the adulterated milk. In the event of granting bail, the accused is likely to commit similar offences. Thus, the bail petition deserves to be rejected. 7. In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in (2011) 1 SCC 694 in the case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre V/s State of Maharashtra and others, one of the parameters that can be taken into consideration while dealing with the anticipatory bail is frivolity in prosecution and the element of genuineness.
